text: The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother.
They played the whore in Egypt; in their youth they played the whore. There their breasts were fondled, and there their maiden breasts were handled.

versions.text: They played the whore in Egypt; in their youth they played the whore. There their breasts were fondled, and there their young bodies were handled.
versions.explanation: The second clause renders דַּדֵּי בְּתוּלֵיהֶן ("the breasts of their virginity") as "their young bodies," which generalizes and loses the parallelism of the Hebrew. "Maiden breasts" keeps the image while remaining readable aloud, and matches the same phrase rendered as "young breasts" in verse 8.

text: Their names were Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. As for their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.

versions.text: Their names were Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. Their names mean this: Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
versions.explanation: "Their names mean this" adds an interpretive gloss not present in the Hebrew, which simply repeats "and their names were." The Hebrew word order also places the city first as the subject of identification.

text: But Oholah played the whore while she was mine. She burned with lust for her lovers, the Assyrians, her neighbors—
governors and commanders dressed in blue, all of them handsome young men, cavalrymen mounted on horses.
She gave herself as a whore to them, the choicest men of Assyria, every one of them; and with all whom she lusted after she defiled herself with their idols.
Nor did she give up the whoring she began in Egypt, for in her youth men had slept with her, had handled her young breasts and poured out their lust on her.
Therefore I handed her over to her lovers, to the Assyrians she lusted after.
They stripped her naked, seized her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and judgment was carried out on her.
Her sister Oholibah saw all this, yet in her lust she was even more corrupt than her sister, and her whoring surpassed her sister's.
She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, her neighbors, splendidly dressed, cavalrymen mounted on horses, all of them handsome young men.
And I saw that she had defiled herself; both of them had gone the same way.
But she carried her whoring still further. She saw men carved on the wall, figures of Chaldeans etched in vermilion,
belts around their waists, flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers—the very image of Babylonians, whose native land is Chaldea.
At the mere sight of them she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
So the Babylonians came to her, to her bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. And when she had been defiled by them, she turned from them in disgust.
When she flaunted her whoring and exposed her nakedness, I turned from her in disgust, just as I had turned from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her whoring, remembering the days of her youth, when she played the whore in the land of Egypt,
and she lusted after her lovers there, whose members were like those of donkeys and whose seed like that of horses.
So you longed again for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your breasts and fondled your young body.
Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to rouse your lovers against you, the very ones you turned from in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side—

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, handsome young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of rank, all of them riding on horses.

They will come against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, and with a horde of peoples. They will surround you with shield and buckler and helmet. I will hand the judgment over to them, and they will judge you by their own laws.

I will turn my jealous anger against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and those left of you will fall by the sword. They will take away your sons and daughters, and what remains of you will be consumed by fire.
They will strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewels.
So I will put an end to your lewdness and to the whoring you began in Egypt. You will not lift your eyes to them again or remember Egypt anymore.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am handing you over to those you hate, to those you turned from in disgust.
They will deal with you in hatred and take everything you have worked for, leaving you stripped and naked. Then the shame of your whoring will be exposed—your lewdness and your promiscuity.
All this comes on you because you played the whore after the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.

versions.text: All this comes on you because you chased after the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
versions.explanation: בִּזְנוֹתֵךְ is the verb for prostitution, consistently rendered "played the whore" elsewhere in the chapter; "chased after" weakens the sexual-covenantal imagery central to the oracle and breaks the chapter's lexical consistency.

text: You have walked in your sister's way, so I will put her cup into your hand.
This is what the Lord GOD says: You will drink your sister's cup, deep and wide; it will bring scorn and ridicule, for it holds so much.
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief—a cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it dry, gnaw its broken pieces, and tear your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have forgotten me and thrust me behind your back, you must bear the weight of your lewdness and your whoring.
The LORD said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then confront them with their abominations.
For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols, and they even offered up the children they had borne to me as food for them.
And this too they did to me: on that same day they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
On the very day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary and profaned it. That is what they did inside my house.
They even sent for men who came from far away. A messenger was sent to them, and they came. And for them you bathed, painted your eyes, and put on your jewelry.
You sat on a stately couch with a table spread before it, and on that table you set my incense and my oil.

versions.text: You reclined on a stately couch with a table spread before it, and on that table you set my incense and my oil.
versions.explanation: יָשַׁבְתְּ means "you sat"; "reclined" adds a posture not in the Hebrew and is not needed for the imagery.

text: The noise of a carefree crowd was around her—men from the great throng, and drunkards brought in from the desert—and they put bracelets on the women's wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.

versions.text: The noise of a carefree crowd surrounded her; men were brought in from the desert along with a great throng, and they put bracelets on the women's wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew word סובאים/סָבָאִים (written form "drunkards," read form "Sabeans") is left untranslated; the current rendering flattens the phrase to a generic "men." A footnote could note the alternate reading "Sabeans." Also, בָהּ is better rendered "around/with her" than "surrounded her."

text: Then I said of the one worn out by adultery: Now they will keep using her as a whore, for that is what she is.
Men went in to her as men go in to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.

versions.text: They went in to her as men go in to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.
versions.explanation: The first verb is singular ("he went in to her"), functioning generically; "Men went in to her" preserves the shift from singular to the plural "they went in" in the second clause.

text: But righteous men will pass sentence on them—the sentence for adulteresses and for women who shed blood—because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: Bring up an assembly against them and hand them over to terror and plunder.
The assembly will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses down.
So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and will not act as you have.
You will be repaid for your lewdness and will bear the guilt of your idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
